topics.title: The journey of food inside us

learn.hook: You eat a bite of idli. Where does it go next? It takes a long trip through a tube many metres long inside you!
points: Digestion is how our body breaks food down into tiny parts that it can use.
In the mouth, teeth cut and chew food. The tongue mixes it with saliva, which makes it soft and wet.
The food pipe carries food from the mouth to the stomach. In the stomach, digestive juices mix with the food and churn it.
In the small intestine, digestion is completed. The useful parts of food go into the blood and reach every part of the body.
The large intestine takes back water from what is left. The waste then leaves the body.

example.q: Chew a piece of plain roti slowly for a long time. It starts to taste a little sweet. Think it through: why?
steps: Roti has a lot of starch.
Saliva in the mouth starts breaking down starch.
Starch is changed into a kind of sugar, so it tastes sweet.
example.answer: Saliva starts changing the starch in roti into sugar.

learn.reallife: That is why elders say 'chew your food well'. Well-chewed food is easier for the stomach and intestines to digest.

games.title: Food's travel route
games.prompt: Put the parts in the order food passes through them

games.title: Teeth at work
pairs: Mixes food with saliva and tastes it

quiz.q: Where does digestion of food begin?
quiz.explain: Digestion starts in the mouth, where teeth chew food and saliva mixes with it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks digestion starts only in the stomach

quiz.q: Which tube carries food from the mouth to the stomach?
quiz.explain: The food pipe carries swallowed food down to the stomach. The wind pipe carries air to the lungs.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the food pipe with the wind pipe

quiz.q: Which teeth are best for grinding food?
quiz.explain: Molars at the back have broad, flat tops for grinding and crushing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sharp front teeth do the grinding

quiz.q: In which part does most of the useful food go into the blood?
quiz.explain: Digestion is completed in the small intestine, and the useful parts of food pass into the blood there.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the stomach or mouth sends food into the blood

quiz.q: What does the large intestine mainly take back from leftover food?
quiz.explain: The large intestine soaks up water from the leftover food. Then the waste leaves the body.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of the large intestine

quiz.q: Saliva helps digestion because it
options: makes food soft and starts breaking down starch
keeps food out of the stomach
quiz.explain: Saliva wets the food so we can swallow it, and starts changing starch into sugar.
quiz.mistake: Thinks saliva is only water with no job

quiz.q: How many milk teeth does a child usually have?
quiz.explain: Children usually have 20 milk teeth. Adults have up to 32 permanent teeth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up milk teeth with adult teeth

quiz.q: Why should we chew food well before swallowing?
options: Small soft pieces are easier to digest
quiz.explain: Chewing breaks food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva, so the stomach and intestines can digest it easily.
quiz.mistake: Thinks chewing does not matter for digestion

teach.ask: Gappu swallows a seed and blinks: 'Where did my seed go? What happens to food inside us?'
teach.praise: Wow! Mouth, food pipe, stomach, then the intestines, and the good parts go into the blood. My seed went on a big trip!
teach.nudge: What happens to food in the mouth first? And where does it go after the stomach?

learn.hook: A plate of dal, rice, sabzi and curd is like a team. Each player has a different job to keep you strong!
points: Food has nutrients, the useful parts that our body needs.
Carbohydrates and fats give us energy. Rice, roti, potato and sugar have carbohydrates. Ghee, oil, butter and nuts have fats.
Proteins help us grow and repair the body. Dal, rajma, eggs, fish, milk and paneer give us proteins.
Vitamins and minerals protect us from illness. Fruits, vegetables and milk give us these. Calcium in milk keeps bones and teeth strong.
Roughage (fibre) in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food move through the body. Water is also very important.

example.q: Kabir plays football for two hours. What should he eat to get energy quickly, and what helps his muscles grow?
steps: Energy comes from carbohydrates and fats.
A roti or a banana gives carbohydrates for energy.
Dal, eggs or paneer give proteins for growth and repair.
example.answer: Carbohydrate foods for energy, and protein foods to help muscles grow.

learn.reallife: Look at your lunch box today. Can you find one energy food, one body-building food and one protective food in it?

items.text: Dal and eggs are rich in ___.
Ghee and oil are rich in ___.
Calcium keeps our bones and ___ strong.
Amla and oranges are rich in vitamin ___.
Our skin makes vitamin D in ___.

quiz.q: Which nutrient mainly gives us energy?
quiz.explain: Carbohydrates in rice, roti and potatoes are the body's main energy food.
quiz.mistake: Thinks vitamins give energy

quiz.q: Which food is rich in proteins?
quiz.explain: Dals and pulses are rich in proteins, which help the body grow and repair itself.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up protein foods with energy foods

quiz.q: Which nutrient helps the body grow and repair itself?
quiz.explain: Proteins are body-building nutrients. They help us grow and heal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks energy foods build the body

quiz.q: Which mineral in milk keeps bones and teeth strong?
quiz.explain: Calcium makes bones and teeth hard and strong. Milk, curd and ragi have calcium.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up calcium with iron

quiz.q: What does roughage (fibre) do for us?
options: Helps food and waste move through the body
Makes us taller in one day
quiz.explain: Fibre does not give much energy, but it helps food move smoothly through the intestines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fibre has no use because it is not digested

quiz.q: Which fruit is very rich in vitamin C?
quiz.explain: Amla (Indian gooseberry) has a lot of vitamin C, which helps keep gums and skin healthy.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fruit known for energy rather than vitamin C

quiz.q: Our body can make vitamin D when our skin gets
quiz.explain: When sunlight falls on our skin, the body makes vitamin D, which helps keep bones strong.
quiz.mistake: Does not know sunlight helps make vitamin D

quiz.q: Which of these foods is rich in fats?
quiz.explain: Butter, ghee, oil and nuts are rich in fats, which also give energy.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fat-rich foods with fruits and vegetables

teach.ask: Gappu pecks at a plate: 'Why can't I just eat sweets all day? What do different foods do?'
teach.praise: Oh! Some foods give energy, some help me grow and some protect me. Sweets alone can't do all that!
teach.nudge: Which foods help us grow? And which foods protect us from falling ill?

topics.title: Balanced diet and healthy food habits

learn.hook: Eating only aloo paratha every day sounds yummy, but your body would miss many things. What does a happy, healthy plate look like?
points: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts, along with water and roughage.
Millets like ragi, bajra and jowar are healthy grains grown in India. The year 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.
Junk food has too much oil, salt or sugar and few useful nutrients. We should eat it only once in a while.
Wash your hands before eating, wash fruits and vegetables, and keep food covered.
Food can be kept from spoiling by keeping it cool, drying it (like papad) or using salt, oil or sugar (like pickles and jam).

example.q: Riya's lunch is two samosas and a cold drink. Think it through: is it a balanced meal? How can she improve it?
steps: Samosas are fried, so they have a lot of fat and carbohydrates.
The cold drink has a lot of sugar.
There is little protein, vitamins or fibre.
She can eat roti with dal, sabzi, salad and a glass of buttermilk instead.
example.answer: It is not balanced. A meal like roti, dal, sabzi, salad and buttermilk is better.

learn.reallife: Many government schools serve hot cooked mid-day meals (the PM POSHAN scheme). These meals include grains, dal and vegetables to keep children healthy.

games.title: Healthy or not?
items: A balanced diet has all nutrients in the right amounts.
Ragi, bajra and jowar are millets.
These are healthy grains grown widely in India.
Eating chips and cold drinks every day is a healthy habit.
They have too much salt, oil and sugar.
We should wash our hands before eating.
Washing removes germs that could make us ill.
Mouldy bread is safe to eat if we remove the green part.
Mould can spread inside food. Mouldy food should be thrown away.

quiz.q: What is a balanced diet?
options: Food with all nutrients in the right amounts
Food eaten while standing on one leg
quiz.explain: A balanced diet gives the body every nutrient it needs, in the right amounts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one nutrient alone is enough

quiz.q: Which of these is a millet?
quiz.explain: Ragi (finger millet) is a millet. Rice and wheat are other grains, and moong is a pulse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every grain is a millet

quiz.q: The year 2023 was celebrated around the world as the International Year of
quiz.explain: The United Nations declared 2023 the International Year of Millets, after India proposed it.
quiz.mistake: Guesses another food famous in India

quiz.q: Why should we eat junk food only once in a while?
options: It has too much oil, salt or sugar and few nutrients
quiz.explain: Junk food fills us up but gives few useful nutrients, and too much fat, salt or sugar is bad for health.
quiz.mistake: Thinks tasty food must also be healthy

quiz.q: Which meal is the most balanced?
options: Roti, dal, mixed sabzi, salad and curd
quiz.explain: It has carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and fibre together.
quiz.mistake: Picks a favourite food instead of a mix of food groups

quiz.q: How are papads kept from spoiling?
options: They are dried in the sun
They are wrapped in wet cloth
They are kept in a warm, damp place
quiz.explain: Drying removes water. Germs that spoil food need water to grow, so dry papads last long.
quiz.mistake: Does not know why drying stops spoiling

quiz.q: Which is a healthy food habit?
options: Eating food left uncovered for flies
quiz.explain: Washing fruits removes dirt and germs, keeping us safe.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how germs get into food

quiz.q: Which is a sign that food has gone bad?
options: It is on a clean plate
It smells bad or has fuzzy mould on it
quiz.explain: A bad smell, a strange taste or mould means germs have spoilt the food.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the signs of spoilt food

teach.ask: Gappu holds a jalebi: 'If jalebis taste so good, why can't I eat only jalebis? What is a balanced diet?'
teach.praise: I get it! A little of everything in the right amounts, and jalebis only sometimes. My tummy says thank you!
teach.nudge: What should a healthy plate have? And why is too much junk food a problem?
